nodes.summary: The decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a precedence-multiprocessor scheduling instance that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The precedence-constrained multiprocessor scheduling decision problem

nodes.summary: An instance $(d, P, m, D)$ with job durations $d = (d_0, \dots, d_{n-1})$ is feasible when there are start times $s_0, \dots, s_{n-1} \in \mathbb{N}$ and machines $\mu_0, \dots, \mu_{n-1} \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\mu_j < m$ and $s_j + d_j \le D$ for every $j < n$, $s_a + d_a \le s_b$ for every precedence pair $(a, b) \in P$, and for all jobs $a < b < n$ with $\mu_a = \mu_b$, either $s_a + d_a \le s_b$ or…
nodes.title: Feasible precedence-multiprocessor scheduling instances

nodes.summary: An instance is a tuple $(d, P, m, D)$ in which $d = (d_0, \dots, d_{n-1})$ is a list of natural numbers, $d_j$ being the duration of job $j$; $P$ is a list of pairs $(a, b)$ of natural numbers, each read as the precedence constraint that job $a$ precedes job $b$; $m$ is a natural number, the number of machines; and $D$ is a natural number, the deadline.
nodes.title: Instances of precedence-constrained multiprocessor scheduling

nodes.summary: The precedence-constrained multiprocessor scheduling decision problem is in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: PRECEDENCE-CONSTRAINED MULTIPROCESSOR SCHEDULING is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance $(d, P, m, D)$ whose list of job durations $d$ has length $n$ is well formed when every precedence pair $(a, b) \in P$ satisfies $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$, and there is an ordering of the jobs $0, \dots, n-1$ (a permutation of this list) in which $a$ comes before $b$ for every $(a, b) \in P$.
nodes.title: Well-formed precedence-multiprocessor scheduling instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
